conventions.convention: Spaces carrying states are nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, with the inner product linear in its first argument.

The followed band consists of full eigenspaces, has constant rank m ≥ 1, and locally continues an isolated cluster. Its gap is the distance to the entire complementary spectrum; the gap is +∞ when the complement is zero.
Slow-time evolution satisfies iU′T(s) = TH(s)UT(s), with UT(0) = I; the path is C², including one-sided endpoint derivatives.

Preparation, coefficient evaluation, term exponentials, inverse and controlled access, precision, queries, description length and generation costs are separately supplied and charged; a missing resource is unavailable.
Circuit products act right to left. The data register precedes the clock, legal clocks are cℓ = 1^ℓ0^(N−ℓ), and the clock is discarded by partial trace.
History-path inputs have n ≥ 1, L ≥ 1 and rational 0 < ε ≤ 1; K = ceil(2L/ε), N = L + K. In particular, the local clock-pattern instructions are only invoked with N ≥ 3.
The reversible-chain bound concerns the algebraic gap 1 − λ₂, not an absolute spectral gap, and assumes irreducibility and a strictly positive stationary probability satisfying detailed balance.

load_bearing.statement: For a C² finite-dimensional Hermitian path with a coherently followed rank-m spectral projection separated by full gap g(s)>0, the projector deviation is at most A_m(s), where A_m is 1/T times the two endpoint terms m‖H′‖/g² plus the integral of m‖H″‖/g² + 7m√m‖H′‖²/g³. Every initially normalized band vector has transition probability at most A_m(s)².

For the stated C² gapped rank-m projection, P′ equals the reduced-resolvent transform of H′; the transform has norm at most √m‖X‖/g, and the stated second-projection and differentiated-transform block estimates hold.
For the constructed history path, Δ₀ = 1/[216(N+1)³] and J = 2K₀ + 4K₀²/Δ₀ + 1 give a unique full-space ground state and gap greater than 3Δ₀/4 for every s ∈ [0,1].

Under the stated availability of coefficient evaluations, supported term-time calls and certified errors, the discretized algorithm produces an evolution block within ε in operator norm of UT(1). Circuit-family expansion additionally requires the stated providers and polynomial-time complete generation.
For N ≥ 1, H₀(s) = (1−s)diag(0,1,…,N) + (s/2)L_N has a simple ground eigenvalue and spectral gap at least 1/(48N²) for every s ∈ [0,1].
For the stated splitting and operator bounds, J>2K gives μ_k−K²/(J−2K) ≤ λ_k(H_J) ≤ μ_k for k=1,2, hence a full gap at least the compressed gap minus K²/(J−2K).
The full final Hamiltonian has the unique normalized history ground state η, and its data marginal is at trace distance at most L/(N+1) ≤ ε/2 from the specified circuit output.
For the stated finite irreducible reversible row-stochastic chain, the algebraic gap satisfies 1−λ₂ ≥ φ²/2.
For density operators ρ,σ on nonzero finite-dimensional H_A ⊗ H_B, D(Tr_B ρ,Tr_B σ) ≤ D(ρ,σ).

concerns.concern: Proof 5.1 establishes that every x orthogonal to v has Rayleigh quotient at least t/(4N²), then says every such quotient is at least E₁−E₀ and concludes E₁−E₀ ≥ t/(4N²). Those two lower bounds alone do not imply the conclusion. Explicitly choose an E₁ eigenvector, whose quotient equals E₁−E₀. This immediately closes the proof without changing the claim.

The Statement says “Take the one-qubit circuit U₁=X, U₂=Z” and calls K=4, N=6 the prescribed padding. The cited construction accepts a full-list uniform circuit under def-qc-uniform-circuit-family, whose gate labels are exactly H,T,T†,CNOT. X and Z therefore require an explicit macro-gate interpretation for this illustration; expanding them into the declared syntax changes the listed gate count and padding. The displayed six-transition history-state calculation itself is correct.
